report.summary: Session chunk 2: Evidence, Claim, TurnRef, ParticipantRecord, CouncilRecord dataclasses and _parse_claims function. Claims about advisory-only, no verdict token, no decision, and verbatim parsing are kept; some about from_patch_artifact and from_files are partially kept or uncheckable.

handoff.purpose: Defines evidence, claim, turn, participant, and council record dataclasses and a claim parser.

symbols.note: Dataclass for evidence with label, paths, files, author_vendor, base_revision, digest.

symbols.name: Evidence.refs
symbols.note: Returns evidence citations: path + sha256 of exact bytes shown.

symbols.name: Evidence.text_tokens
symbols.note: Returns sum of token counts for all file texts.

symbols.note: Dataclass for one assertion by one participant.

symbols.name: _parse_claims
symbols.note: Splits response into Claim objects, keeping bytes verbatim.

claims.text: Neither is ever concatenated before scanning.
claims.why: Refers to something outside this chunk (likely previous code).

claims.text: author_vendor names the vendor that WROTE the material, so a council seat held by that same vendor is flagged self_review on every one of its turns.
claims.why: The self_review flag exists in TurnRef but the logic to set it is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Evidence citations: path + sha256 of the EXACT bytes shown. Two participants citing "the file" may have been shown different bytes; without the digest the transcript records a citation nobody can reproduce.
claims.why: refs() returns tuple of evidence_ref(path, encoded text) which includes the digest.

claims.text: From spine.attempt.PatchArtifact -- the first intended input. changed_paths becomes the path channel; the diff itself is shown as one evidence file so the content channel scans it whole-file, per the floor's own contract.
claims.why: The method sets paths from artifact.changed_paths and files to ('PATCH.diff', diff). The 'floor's own contract' is uncheckable.

claims.text: Read files off disk as evidence. Unreadable files are NAMED, never silently dropped -- a missing evidence file that reads as an empty one is a council reviewing something other than what it says it reviewed.
claims.why: The method catches OSError and adds a placeholder with the error type, so files are never silently dropped.

claims.text: One assertion by one participant, VERBATIM. checkable is true only when the author supplied a concrete deterministic check -- a command, a test, a specific line assertion. That is the council's entire product: a queue of checks for the gate to run. A claim without one is still recorded verbatim, and still counts for nothing on its own.
claims.why: Claim dataclass has fields checkable and check; docstring describes their semantics.

claims.text: The council's output. ADVISORY. It promotes nothing. There is deliberately no majority, no score, no consensus and no approve/reject field, and none may be added: a caller must not be able to destructure a decision out of this object. What is here instead is every claim with its author and its evidence, the checkable subset, and honest roster accounting.
claims.why: CouncilRecord has no such fields; __post_init__ enforces advisory=True.

claims.text: Always True and enforced. This object is evidence, not a decision.
claims.why: advisory defaults to True and __post_init__ raises if set to False.

claims.text: The queue the gate can actually run.
claims.why: Returns tuple of claims where c.checkable is True.

claims.text: Never a bare fraction. "3 of 4" and "2 of 2" must not be able to render as the same thing.
claims.why: The property returns a string with responded, requested, distinct_classes; the rendering format ensures distinction, but the claim about 'not the same' is a design intent that cannot be fully verified without seeing all possible inputs.

claims.text: Human rendering. The degraded flag sits ADJACENT TO THE FINDINGS -- never in a footer, where a reader takes a two-vendor council for four.
claims.why: render() places the degraded flag on the quorum line, not in a footer.

claims.text: Split a response into claims, keeping every byte VERBATIM. A vendor that ignores the format is NOT summarised and NOT dropped: its whole answer becomes one parsed=False claim. Summarising dissent is the failure this module exists to avoid, so the parser never paraphrases.
claims.why: If no lines match _CLAIM_RE, returns a single Claim with parsed=False.

claims.text: The transcript will not say so unless the record makes it.
claims.why: Refers to transcript behavior outside this chunk.

observations.what: Evidence.from_patch_artifact uses getattr to access artifact attributes; no validation that artifact is a PatchArtifact.
Evidence.from_files reads files with errors='replace' and no size limit; large files could cause memory issues.
CouncilRecord.__post_init__ enforces advisory=True but does not enforce other invariants like chain_intact consistency.
